independence_declaration.statement: qa-verifier authored no product implementation in the DG2 scope. This round I wrote only QA tests and evidence: the R17 specs docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/tests/round-17/e2e/dg2-qa-r17.spec.ts and dg2-qa-r17-diag.spec.ts (outside the candidate, because the candidate is frozen), the evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/round-17/, and this record, its verifications sidecar and its narrative. The round-17 repair FE15 (ac81298, D-077) is frontend-ux-engineer's. Every result comes from my own runs in three disposable clones of the source commit 805da3e2 under $TMPDIR (review-dg2, review-dg2-e2e, review-dg2-diag), all removed at the end together with the test scratch. HEAD was 23edabfb at the start, the round-17 freeze and assignment commit (a child of 805da3e2 that touches only the three round-17 assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json). During my run HEAD moved to 7937c78b through the other reviewers' auto-committed round-17 runs and evidence. A `git diff --name-only` showed me the NAMES of code-security's round-17 files (00-candidate.log); I did not open any of them, nor any other reviewer's round-17 record or evidence. None of the 181 files changed in 805da3e2..HEAD is among the 564 manifest entries. The candidate ID recomputes as sha256:ddaab3cc... with 564 files at the start and at the end, on HEAD, at --ref 805da3e2 and in each clone. Of the validate --reconcile output I read only the structure and per-round status lines (round 17: all three missing at that time). I formed this verdict from my own runs.

THE 2 FAILURES, the same in both settings and both projects, are my own round-15 test R15-04, at its LAST step only (dg2-qa-r15.spec.ts line 428). After the in-app navigation it expected the second language switch to show the 'not saved' notice again, and the notice is absent ('element(s) not found'). Every earlier R15-04 assertion passed in all 4 runs. Those are the real 403 csrf, the notice in the shown language, staying signed in on /transformations with A's list rendered, the route-replaced 403 detail read not being a session end, Back rendering the list, and /me <= 2. Investigated in QA-R17-20, it is measured, not guessed. FE15's /me confirmation on that in-app navigation (D-077 (3)) returned the same person with the new session's CSRF token, so the second save carried the new token and was ANSWERED 200, and the preference was persisted. Showing no 'not saved' notice is then the correct outcome. R15-04's last step encoded the pre-FE15 assumption that the stale token persists until a refocus. That makes it an obsolete expectation in my test, not a product regression, and R17-10 supersedes it. No other test failed. The other error-looking lines are the failure output of those 2 tests, R17-08's deliberate 403 csrf measurement line, 3 npm .npmrc warnings, and the measurement lines of passing R9/R11/R12/R13 tests. Examples are R9-06's 400 bodies, and R12-06's 'console errors/warnings 6', which are its expected 401/400/404 resource loads.

Each locale setting, chromium-en and chromium-ar.
checks_run.command: <locale env> e2e/support/qa-stack.sh npx playwright test e2e/dg2-qa-r17-diag.spec.ts e2e/dg2-qa-r15.spec.ts --grep 'R17-10|R15-04' --workers=1

checks_run.expected: the cause of the R15-04 failure is measured. If the second save is 2xx with the new token, there is no notice, and the preference persists, the change is intended (not a regression). If the second save is 403 without a notice, that is a regression and becomes a finding.
checks_run.actual: In both settings and both projects (exit 1 by design: R15-04 fails 4/4 at line 428 exactly as in the full runs; R17-10 passes 4/4) the measured sequence is the same. The page's /me returns csrf X. The same person signs in again, and the first PUT carries X and is answered 403 csrf, with the notice shown, still signed in. The in-app navigation's /me returns the same person with csrf Y. The second PUT carries Y and is answered 200, with 0 notices and the server's preferredLocale equal to the language chosen. There were 2 /me since the re-sign-in. Example (unset, EN): csrf Ka12P0c0... -> 403, then TP1gUUQO... -> 200. The conclusion is that the missing notice is correct and FE11/FE12's guarantees hold: a 403 is never a session end, and a REFUSED save shows the notice in the shown language. No finding.
